data.description:
## The defect

The Dependency Advisory Canary **force-closes an open p1 vulnerability ticket when `pip-audit`
CRASHES**, with a message asserting the advisories cleared, and the workflow run stays GREEN.

"The audit could not run" and "there are no vulnerabilities" are the same input to this code.

## Mechanism, verified in source on current `origin/main`

`scripts/dependency_audit.py:488`

```python
blocking = environ.get("BLOCKING", "false") == "true"
```

`BLOCKING` is `${{ steps.audit.outputs.blocking }}`. The audit step
(`.github/workflows/dependency-advisory-canary.yml:134`) is **`continue-on-error: true`** and runs
under `set -uo pipefail` — deliberately, so a blocking verdict does not skip escalation. But if the
step CRASHES it sets no output, `BLOCKING` arrives as `""`, and `"" == "true"` is `False`.

`not blocking` then selects the close arm at `:537-560`, which runs:

```python
"rebar", "transition", tid, "open", "closed",
"--class", "env_integration",
"--reason", f"Fixed: dependency advisories cleared on main at {ts}.",
f"--force={force_close}",
```

Note this is an automated **`--force`**, the same override AGENTS.md forbids agents from using.

## PROVEN by execution, no production contact

I drove `cmd_advisory_alert` directly with a stub runner and a stubbed `alert_dedup` so an open
advisory ticket "exists", varying only the `BLOCKING` environment:

```
Scenario: an OPEN dependency-advisory ticket exists.

  audit CRASHED (BLOCKING output never set)    rc=0  cmds=1  FORCE-CLOSE=YES
  audit CRASHED (BLOCKING='')                  rc=0  cmds=1  FORCE-CLOSE=YES
  audit ran, advisories genuinely cleared      rc=0  cmds=1  FORCE-CLOSE=YES   <- IDENTICAL
  audit ran, advisory STILL blocking           rc=0  cmds=1  FORCE-CLOSE=no    (correct)
```

The crash case and the genuine all-clear emit a **byte-identical** command, including the reason
text "Fixed: dependency advisories cleared at <ts>". Nothing downstream can tell them apart, and
the ticket that recorded the vulnerability is gone.

## The asymmetry that shows this was an oversight, not a decision

The same function ALREADY guards the opposite direction, twelve lines above (`:495-500`):

```python
if blocking and not ids.strip():
    print("::error::advisory-alert invoked blocking with no advisory ids — refusing to "
          "file a hollow ticket. Fix the gate wiring.")
    return 1
```

So the author explicitly refused to FILE a hollow ticket on missing data — and did not apply the
same reasoning to CLOSING one on missing data. Filing a spurious ticket is noise; closing a real
vulnerability ticket destroys the signal. The guarded direction is the harmless one.

## Exposure: LATENT — it has not fired, and I checked

- No `[dependency-advisory]` alert ticket exists in the store, so there has been nothing to close.
- All eight most recent canary runs (2026-08-29 through 2026-09-05) concluded **success**.

Firing requires BOTH an open advisory ticket AND an audit crash. Neither has coincided. Filed p1
on severity and on the fact that the lane runs daily against a security signal, not on any observed
loss — stating that plainly so nobody hunts for a destroyed ticket that does not exist.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A crashed or non-running audit is DISTINGUISHABLE from a clean audit at the close decision.
      An absent/empty `BLOCKING` must not select the close arm. Decide deliberately whether it
      should error, no-op, or comment — and record why.
- [ ] The workflow does not report SUCCESS when the audit step did not produce a verdict. The
      `continue-on-error: true` is there for a stated reason (not skipping escalation); preserve
      that reason while making a crash visible.
- [ ] Closing an advisory ticket does NOT use `--force`. If advisory tickets genuinely have no
      completion criteria to verify, that is an argument for giving them a disposition path, not
      for automating the override that exists for human judgement.
- [ ] A regression test drives `cmd_advisory_alert` with `BLOCKING` unset, `""`, `"false"` and
      `"true"` against a stubbed open ticket and pins which of them may close it. Seed the defect
      by reverting the fix and confirm it goes RED — a test that passes both before and after
      would be this ticket's own bug class.
- [ ] The same `environ.get(KEY, "false") == "true"` shape is swept for across the repo's CI
      scripts, and each instance is recorded as safe or fixed. Enumerate the result; this is a
      pattern, not a one-off.
data.title: Dependency Advisory Canary force-closes an open p1 vulnerability ticket when pip-audit CRASHES, asserting 'advisories cleared', with the run green -- a crashed audit is byte-identical to a clean one
